title: Model normal lease expiry and clock interpretation

git.kind: git archive of exact commit; no Git metadata

findings.invariant: A dead holder's lease whose heartbeat is older than 3 × HEARTBEAT is reclaimable (RFC 0002 §9.7.3).
findings.evidence: Existing test acquires as pid 11 boot-a then challenges as pid 22 boot-b at +60s. isBusy returns false at leases.ts:106-110 because real boot ids differ, before ageSeconds. Executed 2026-09-06T22:00:11Z: 7 existing tests pass, including this one, without covering same-boot dead PID at 29s/30s/31s.
findings.required_fix: P020 land same-boot dead-holder fixed-timestamp cases from /work/out/leases-expiry.test.ts. Do not treat leases.test.ts:84-94 as heartbeat-window proof.

findings.invariant: RFC wording is older than / past 3 × heartbeat. Qualification uses millisecond strict greater-than against row ttl_s.
findings.evidence: Replica and draft: T0 to T0+30000ms, dead same-boot → acquireLease reason reclaimed (draft test passed). Qualification replica at 30000ms is ok, not lease-stale. RFC expected under strict older-than is still busy.
findings.required_fix: P020 keep or change the inclusive 30s boundary explicitly. Do not silently rely on floor(ms/1000) < 30.

findings.invariant: Schema stores ttl_s; reclaim math uses HEARTBEAT_SECONDS * LEASE_RECLAIM_HEARTBEATS only.
findings.evidence: Draft test stored ttl_s=1, dead same-boot, age 5s → busy; row ttl_s remained 1. Qualification would emit lease-stale for ttl_s=1 at 5s.
findings.required_fix: P020/P091 document or wire ttl_s; do not assume the column is the reclaim window.

findings.invariant: Unparseable times must not justify a steal. RFC3339 leap seconds are legal in isRfc3339.
findings.evidence: Bun 1.3.14 Date.parse('2026-06-30T23:59:60Z') is NaN → ageSeconds 0 → busy. qualificationDate requires ^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$. Lease reclaim does not call isRfc3339.
